answer:
**A follow-up often omits slots supplied by the conversation.** After “What was Apple's Q3 revenue?”, “What about Microsoft?” changes the entity while retaining the metric and intended period. Searching only the literal second sentence loses those constraints. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)

Create a standalone query using structured conversation state: entity, metric, year, period, currency, and comparison intent. Preserve the original utterance and retrieve with both forms when useful.

**Inherited context can itself be ambiguous.** Companies may have different fiscal quarters. A comparison of each company's fiscal Q3 is not necessarily a comparison over the same calendar months. Resolve the intended period or state the interpretation clearly, and cite the underlying reports.

Do not silently invent a year or change revenue to profit. Test pronouns, entity swaps, topic changes, and corrections separately from retrieval quality. A rewriting model can produce a fluent but wrong query; validate important slots before treating the rewrite as the user's request. Conversational retrieval succeeds when omitted context is restored accurately, not merely when the query becomes longer.

**Technical details and references.**

Rewrite the follow-up using conversation state: after “What was Apple's Q3 revenue?”, “What about Microsoft?” means Microsoft's revenue for the relevant Q3, not a generic Microsoft search. Preserve the requested metric, units, year, and comparison intent. Fiscal quarters differ between companies, so resolve whether the user means each company's fiscal Q3 or a shared calendar period before making a comparison. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)

Retrieve using both the standalone rewrite and the original utterance when useful. Store structured slots and source dates; do not silently inherit an unsupported year or replace revenue with profit. Show the period in the answer and cite each company's underlying report. Test entity changes, pronouns, topic switches, and conflicting conversational assumptions separately from retrieval quality.
